capabilities: Execute fenced code blocks via a floating Run button or command palette
Render rich output panels (MIME bundles, Graphviz SVG, D3, Plotly, Cytoscape) beneath blocks
Run blocks in Docker, Podman, WSL, SSH, or QEMU execution groups
Write output to files, pipe stdin, and add interactive slider/select/button input controls
Hash, snapshot, and cryptographically sign notes for reproducibility, with JSONL logging
extras: Executes code locally without sandboxing by default and shows a consent modal; desktop-only because it uses Node.js and local processes. Detailed guides live in the plugin's docs/ directory rather than the README.
motivation: Built for research and exploratory notes where code, proofs, solver queries, and runtime output should stay readable in the document.
problem: Obsidian code blocks are static text with syntax highlighting only; there is no built-in way to execute them and see their output without leaving the note or rewriting the block into a special format.

relations.evidence: Display outputs use MIME bundles inspired by Jupyter outputs.
The built in Godbolt execution group posts snippet source to Compiler Explorer and returns a public shortlink.

requires.name: Docker, Podman, WSL, SSH, or QEMU for execution groups

summary: Code execution plugin that runs standard fenced Markdown code blocks in place, rendering output beneath them while keeping native syntax highlighting.
